arcs.title: El Viejo
arcs.premise: A 41-year-old keeper who won't retire, and his son Teo, who keeps goal for the other side.

outline.beat: The final: broken hand, penalty save, scores from his own box past his own son.
Same night from Teo's POV: why he went up for the corner, the sprint back, the moment he saw who kicked it. Twist: he let himself be beaten? (leave ambiguous).
Flashback: why 'TEO' is written on the tape. Years earlier, El Viejo missed his son's first match for a game of his own and has written the name on his tape every match since.
Next season: Teo's club offers El Viejo a goalkeeper-coach job. To take it he must retire. Twist: he says no, then turns up at training anyway.
Father vs son again, in a penalty shootout. El Viejo has to take the final kick against Teo.
Arc finale: El Viejo retires on the pitch and hands Teo his taped gloves. Loop back to the net-ripple image.

arcs.title: Night Shift Rules
arcs.premise: You (POV) take the night shift at the Wren Motel. The manager, Mr. Hale, left a list of rules. Something that wears Hale's shape (the Visitor) tests every rule. Each episode ends on an A/B choice; the most comment votes decides the next episode.
rules_note: 1. Never open the office door after 3 a.m.
2. Room 9 is empty. If its light is on, don't look.
3. If someone says your name, don't answer.
P.S. I always have my key.
arcs.plan: Loose 6-episode arc; votes bend it. Ideas to draw on: Room 9's light (rule 2), someone calling your name (rule 3), the real Hale arriving with his key, the CCTV room, the torn bottom half of the rules note, the parking lot at 4 a.m., dawn as the finish line (survive until 6 a.m.). Finale vote decides the ending.

outline.beat: Rule 1. 3:00 a.m., three knocks, Hale's voice: 'I forgot my key.' Peephole: Hale far down the hall, back turned. Then its face at the lens. Vote: A open the door / B don't.
